page: Microsoft Azure E8s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance driven by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and virtualized through Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 8 dedicated vCPUs split across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache pool. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX-512 vector acceleration, AVX512_VNNI, and hardware-level AES cryptographic primitives.

System memory totals 64.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no bundled local storage, necessitating network-attached persistent storage for filesystem needs, and contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators. In benchmark assessments, the E8s_v4 produces median-tier performance across multi-threaded applications, scoring 8,469.96 in PassMark CPU tests and sustaining 6.72 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, single-thread compute and uncached memory bandwidth show comparatively lower throughput, with uncached large-block read operations measuring 29.42 GB/sec and write operations achieving 24.3 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration trades high per-core burst velocity and local ephemeral disk IO for concentrated RAM density. This resource profile offers cost efficiency for memory-constrained workloads by avoiding expenditures on unneeded local storage or GPU hardware. The instance is suited for hosting medium-scale relational databases, Redis or Memcached in-memory caching nodes, enterprise ERP systems, and data processing tasks requiring substantial working memory relative to compute allocation.
